Subject: Renewal: Options to lock pricing for 2027

Hi Jordan,

Hope you had a good weekend — we're starting our renewal planning for Redwood and want to understand options to lock pricing for 2027. Usage has ramped faster than we forecasted (embedding and generation traffic up ~55% Y/Y) and we're worried about vendor rate creep next year.

Would Redwood consider multi-year prepay or a staged prepay + true-up model so we can get a fixed effective unit price? Procurement wants to see:
- concrete discount bands by term and prepay level (1yr / 2yr / 3yr)
- an example ramp schedule and how true-ups are handled
- invoicing cadence (annual upfront vs tranche-based invoicing)
- any guardrails (usage caps, overage rates, credits)

Our timeline: legal/procurement needs a term sheet by Nov 12 to slot into next month’s vendor review. Can you send options and any examples you’ve done for similar-scale customers?

Thanks,
Anna Chen
Head of Cloud Operations
CloudSpark Inc

Anna — thanks for the note and the timeline. High level: we can absolutely put together multi-year prepay structures that produce a guaranteed effective unit price while still allowing for a degree of consumption growth via true-up mechanics. Attached is a one-pager with three feasible options tailored for CloudSpark.

Summary (examples, illustrative):

Option A — Annual Prepay (1 year):
- Prepay 100% of estimated annual consumption up front
- Discount: ~12% off list per-token price
- True-up at year-end (overage billed at discounted overage rate)
- Best for predictable consumption and max discount availability

Option B — Staggered Prepay + True-up (2 year):
- Year 1: 40% prepay up front, Year 2: 60% prepay at start of year 2
- Combined term discount: ~20% effective discount vs list across 2 years
- Quarterly true-ups applied against the credit bank; overage charged at pre-agreed rate
- Offers more cash-smoothing while locking rate for both years

Option C — Multi-year Hybrid (3 year):
- Year 1: 30% prepay, Year 2: 35% prepay, Year 3: 35% prepay
- Effective multi-year discount: ~25–28% depending on upfront level
- Quarterly measurement and true-up; unused credits roll forward within term
- Optional capacity carve-outs (reserved GPU pools) for burst needs

Key mechanics and notes:
- True-up: measured monthly, invoiced quarterly to hit a net true-up at each quarter; unused credits carry forward but expire at term end unless renewed.
- Overage rates: pre-agreed tiered bands — if you exceed X% above forecast we apply an incremental overage discounted band rather than list to protect you from sticker shock.
- Invoicing: we can do annual upfront invoice, two-tranche (60/40), or quarterly billing against a credit bank.
- SLA credits: standard SLA credit schedule provided; enhanced SLAs require exec approval.

Attached: prepay_options_CloudSpark_v1.pdf (detailed diagrams, example math, invoice templates).

Next steps: which option do you prefer as a starting point? Also tell us whether procurement prefers a single invoice (wired) vs PO + net30. I can pull Laura (finance) into the contract specifics and Rishi can scope any reserved capacity carve-outs.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Jordan — procurement here. Thanks for the clear options. A few clarifying questions before we escalate to legal:

1) Payment terms — we prefer net45 but can do net30 for partial upfronts. Will Redwood accept a 60% initial deposit followed by scheduled invoices (we can do 60/40 split)?
2) True-up timing — can true-ups be quarterly but with a maximum mid-quarter buffer (i.e., cap invoices to 120% of forecast until true-up settles)?
3) Credit bank vs escrow — can unused credits be held in a Redwood-managed credit bank or do you support an escrow-like structure for larger deposits?
4) SLA credits — we'll request a modest service credit for any P1 downtime beyond the SLA threshold; are you open to a capped financial credit tied to uptime %?
5) Contract redlines — attached is a draft PO and a handful of commercial redlines around payment timing and termination. Can you confirm any clauses you cannot agree to?

Our timelines: procurement committee meets Nov 15; legal needs final commercial terms by Nov 19. If possible we'd like to close in late Nov.

Thanks,
Procurement Ops
CloudSpark Inc

Procurement team — thanks for the careful read and the draft PO. High-level responses inline below and attached is our proposed SOW/terms with tracked changes.

1) Payment terms / 60% deposit: accepted. We can structure: 60% initial deposit (wire), 30% at 12 months, 10% true-up at term close — or, if you prefer, 60/40 over two invoices. Net30 payment on each invoice; net45 requires exec approval but we can consider for enterprise finance programs.

2) True-up cap: we can cap interim invoices at 120% of forecast as an interim protection; final true-up will reconcile to actuals at quarter or term boundaries. We will include a clause for a quarterly true-up settlement.

3) Credit bank vs escrow: Redwood provides a managed credit bank by default; for larger deposits we can accommodate escrow arrangements but that will add a nominal administrative fee and require our legal team to sign an escrow addendum.

4) SLA credits: standard SLA schedule included in the attachment. For additional financial credits you requested, we can agree to a capped P1 credit (suggested cap: 5% of quarterly bill) — anything above that requires exec sign-off. Please confirm the cap you'd want and we'll try to accommodate.

5) Contract redlines: most commercial redlines are acceptable; the only outstanding items needing internal sign-off are extended payment terms >45 days and removal of our termination-for-convenience clause. Laura (cc'd) will follow up on invoicing workflow and PO acceptance.

Next steps:
- We've attached a redlined SOW/terms (proposed_sow_and_terms_redline.pdf).
- If these responses align, please confirm the option you'd like to pursue (A / B / C) and preferred invoice cadence. We'll prepare a DocuSign envelope and route for signatures.
